title: Drtikol: Photographs / Fotografie

description.main: Exhibition catalogue of František Drtikol's studio nudes of 1913 to 1935, edited by Annette and Rudolf Kicken for shows in Prague, Duderstadt and Erfurt. 104 pages, 128 illustrations, English and German text, essays by Vladimír Birgus, Anna Fárová and Matthew S. Witkovsky.
description.extended:
The studio nudes František Drtikol made in Prague between the wars, gathered by Kicken Berlin for a touring exhibition and printed as a large bilingual hardcover.

Annette and Rudolf Kicken edited the book for Hatje Cantz. It accompanied shows at GASK in Prague in 2010, at the Kunsthalle HGN in Duderstadt from December 2011, where Drtikol hung alongside Helmut Newton, and at the Angermuseum in Erfurt in 2012. Rudolf Kicken curated all three shows. It runs to 104 pages with 128 illustrations and two foldout plates, in English and German, with essays by Vladimír Birgus, Anna Fárová and Matthew S. Witkovsky. The plates cover 1913 to 1935. Early nudes posed as nymphs and femmes fatales give way to the geometric studio compositions of the 1920s, with painted cut-out props, raking light and poses taken from dance. Salome, Magdalene and crucifixion subjects follow, and then the late paper-cut silhouettes that replaced live models.

Drtikol (1883–1961) was the first Czech photographer with an international reputation. He gave up the camera in 1935 and was largely forgotten until Anna Fárová's 1972 exhibition in Prague. Her 1986 Schirmer/Mosel monograph fixed the label she gave him, the photographer of Art Deco. His formal vocabulary drew on Futurism, Expressionism and Cubism, and the nude is where he worked it out.
description.artist_bio: František Drtikol (1883–1961), Prague portrait and nude photographer, the first Czech photographer with an international reputation; gave up photography in 1935; rediscovered through Anna Fárová's 1972 Prague exhibition.
description.exhibition_context: Galerie Středočeského kraje (GASK), Prague, May–August 2010; Kunsthalle HGN Duderstadt, from December 2011 (paired with Helmut Newton); Angermuseum Erfurt, 22 July–23 September 2012. All curated by Rudolf Kicken.
